The pedestrian’s statement is admissible as an excited utterance (or present sense impression) because it was made immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was still under the stress of observing it. The pedestrian’s unavailability and lack of identification do not bar admission under the excited utterance exception. However, it is not admissible as a statement of a then-existing mental, emotional, or physical condition if offered to prove the man’s negligence, since it is an opinion about fault rather than a factual observation.  
CONFIDENCE: 70
